summary.name: tinc
summary.one_liner: tinc is a free, open-source VPN daemon that creates encrypted private networks between hosts over the Internet using tunnelling.
use_cases: connect hosts across the internet in a private network
play LAN-only games over the internet
tunnel IPv6 traffic over IPv4 or IPv6 networks
summary.what_it_does: tinc is a VPN daemon that uses tunnelling and encryption to create a private network between hosts on the Internet. It presents the VPN to the IP network layer as a normal network device, so existing software needs no changes. Traffic can be compressed with zlib or LZO and is encrypted with LibreSSL or OpenSSL, with message authentication codes and sequence numbers. It routes traffic over a full mesh, sending packets directly to the destination when possible, and performs NAT traversal when at least one node accepts incoming connections. Adding nodes requires only a new configuration file.
notable: Automatic full mesh routing with direct peer-to-peer paths when possible
NAT traversal when one node has a public incoming address, even dynamic
Adding nodes needs only a config file, no new daemons or interfaces

caveats: Page says version 1.0.37 is likely the last 1.0 release; the 1.1 branch is still in prerelease (1.1pre18)
Drops support for Linux ethertap devices in 1.0.37
Windows support listed covers Windows 2000 through 8 and Windows 7 and 8 specifically; the page notes port state varies by platform
